events.description: Inflation data for Tokyo, published about three weeks ahead of the nationwide figure and widely used as a leading indicator for Japan wide price pressure. Released hours ahead of the Bank of Japan's own decision, it can shift expectations for future rate hikes and move the yen.

events.event: China NBS Manufacturing and Non-Manufacturing PMI (July)
events.revisedNote: The official July manufacturing print came in at 49.2, well below the 50.0 consensus and June's 50.3 reading, confirming a slide back into contraction.
events.description: China's official, government compiled gauges of manufacturing and services and construction activity, released on the last day of the month. A reading above 50 signals expansion, below signals contraction. Among the more closely watched early signals of Chinese economic health, which matters for AUD and NZD as much as CNY given trade links.

events.revisedNote: The Q2 print surged to 1.3% quarter on quarter, up sharply from Q1's 0.4% pace.
events.description: The Australian Bureau of Statistics' quarterly measure of price changes faced by producers before they reach consumers. A slower moving gauge than the CPI, but one the RBA watches for early signs of cost pressures building through supply chains, particularly relevant given the Bank's recent focus on upside inflation risks.

events.event: Bank of Japan interest rate decision
events.description: The Bank of Japan held its policy rate at 1.00% by an 8-1 vote, matching consensus. Board member Hajime Takata dissented, arguing for an immediate hike to 1.25%. The Bank flagged that underlying inflation is likely to move clearly above its 2% target from the second half of the fiscal year, citing wage rises, oil prices and yen weakness, all of which keeps the door open to further tightening later this year.

Nationwide Building Society's monthly gauge of UK house prices, based on its own mortgage lending data. Annual growth slowed to 1.8% in July, with prices up a modest 0.1% on the month, pointing to a cooling but still positive housing market that feeds into the Bank of England's wider view of household demand.

Governor Kazuo Ueda explains the Bank's decision and answers questions from the press. Often moves the yen more than the decision itself, particularly any comments on the timing of the next hike given the dissent in favour of immediate tightening and the yen's recent weakness.

events.event: SARB Governor Kganyago speaks at Reserve Bank AGM
events.description: Governor Lesetja Kganyago addresses the South African Reserve Bank's Ordinary Annual General Meeting of shareholders. As the SARB's chief policymaker, his remarks on inflation and the rand are watched for signals ahead of the next Monetary Policy Committee meeting in September.

events.event: Canada GDP by industry (May, with June advance estimate)
events.description: Statistics Canada's monthly measure of economic output by industry. Released with a roughly two month lag, it gives an early read on how the Canadian economy is tracking heading into the third quarter, at a time when the Bank of Canada has no meeting scheduled until early September.

An early estimate of Eurozone wide inflation for the month. One of the key inputs into the ECB's interest rate decisions and a regular source of euro volatility on release, with today's expected rebound driven mainly by higher energy prices, while core inflation is seen holding near 2.4%.

A regional survey of purchasing managers in the Chicago area, used as an early signal for the following week's national ISM manufacturing survey. Usually a modest, secondary market mover for the dollar.

events.event: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (July, final)
events.description: The final revision of the University of Michigan's survey of US household sentiment, including its closely watched inflation expectations components. Rarely a major mover on its own since the preliminary reading is already known, but the inflation expectations gauge is watched closely by the Fed.

A private sector survey of Chinese manufacturing activity, skewed toward smaller, export and tech oriented firms, released a few days after the official NBS PMI. Often diverges from the official gauge and is watched as a cross check on the health of China's factory sector, with knock on relevance for AUD and NZD.

A survey of purchasing managers in South Africa's manufacturing sector, compiled by Absa and the Bureau for Economic Research and usually published on the first business day of the month. A reading above 50 signals expansion, and a below consensus print tends to weigh on the rand given the sector's fragile recent run.

Switzerland's headline inflation reading from the Federal Statistical Office. With Swiss inflation running well below other major economies, this feeds directly into the SNB's assessment of whether its current policy stance remains appropriate, and is one of the few scheduled CHF data points before the Bank's next quarterly decision in September.

The final, revised reading of S&P Global's Eurozone manufacturing survey, usually only a small adjustment from the flash estimate published earlier in the month. A confirmation style release that rarely moves the euro much on its own.

The final, revised reading of S&P Global's UK manufacturing survey, following a flash estimate of 52.8 for July. Like its Eurozone counterpart, this is usually a modest revision to the flash figure and a secondary mover for sterling.

events.revisedNote: June's reading has been confirmed at 53.3, down from the previously reported 53.8, with the employment sub-index still stuck in contraction.
events.description: The Institute for Supply Management's survey of US manufacturing activity, released on the first business day of the month. A reading above 50 signals expansion. Watched as an early, broad based signal of US industrial health, with markets also focused on the prices paid and new orders sub-indices for clues on inflation and demand.

The British Retail Consortium's monthly gauge of average shop prices, published around ten days ahead of the official ONS inflation figures. A useful early steer on the direction of UK consumer price pressure, though it rarely moves sterling much on its own.

A monthly measure of UK retail sales growth compiled by the British Retail Consortium and KPMG, released a few weeks ahead of the official ONS retail sales figures. Gives an early, if noisy, read on the health of the UK consumer.

S&P Global's survey of activity in the UK construction sector. Housebuilding has been the weakest part of the industry recently, with June's reading barely above May's six year low, so this is watched for signs of whether that drag is easing. Typically a minor mover for sterling.

Statistics Canada's monthly snapshot of the gap between exports and imports of goods. With a large share of Canadian trade tied to the US, this is watched as a barometer of cross border demand and, indirectly, of how tariff related frictions are feeding through to the loonie.

The Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, a measure of unfilled positions across the US economy that the Federal Reserve watches closely as a gauge of labour market slack. A drop toward pre pandemic levels would support the case for further Fed easing.

A broader measure of new orders placed with US manufacturers than the durable goods report released a few days earlier. Usually a secondary market mover, since much of the durable goods component is already known by the time this is published.

events.event: New Zealand employment change and unemployment rate (Q2)
events.description: Stats NZ's quarterly snapshot of the labour market, covering the change in the number of people employed and the jobless rate. It lands just weeks after the RBNZ pivoted back to a hawkish stance and began a fresh tightening cycle, so a soft print would raise questions about how much further the Bank can realistically tighten without hurting employment.

The detailed record of policymakers' discussion from the Bank of Japan's June meeting, published with the usual roughly six week lag. Read for clues on how close the Board was to hiking before this week's actual decision, and on the depth of the dissent for tightening.

A private sector survey of activity in China's much larger services sector, released a few days after the manufacturing equivalent. Rounds out the picture from the official PMIs and the manufacturing Caixin print, with relevance for AUD and NZD given trade links to China.

events.event: Eurozone final services and composite PMI (July)
events.description: The final, revised readings of S&P Global's Eurozone services and composite surveys. Usually only a small adjustment from the flash estimate, and a secondary mover for the euro compared with the manufacturing print.

A measure of the prices charged by Eurozone producers at the factory gate, seen as a leading indicator for future consumer price inflation. Less market moving than the CPI print, but still watched by the ECB as part of its broader inflation picture.

The final, revised reading of S&P Global's UK services survey, covering the much larger part of the UK economy than manufacturing. Confirms or slightly adjusts the flash estimate published earlier in the month, after June marked the sector's steepest contraction since January 2023.

events.revisedNote: June's ADP print has been corrected to 98,000. An earlier update had incorrectly shown 57,000 against this event, which was in fact the same month's official Nonfarm Payrolls figure rather than the ADP number.
events.description: ADP's estimate of private sector payroll growth, released two days ahead of the official US jobs report. Watched closely as an early, if imperfect, signal of how Friday's Nonfarm Payrolls report might land, at a time when the labour market has been showing signs of cooling.

The Institute for Supply Management's survey of the much larger US services sector, released on the third business day of the month. June's reading of 54.0 kept the sector in expansion; a reading above 50 signals growth, with market pricing split fairly evenly between a reading in the low 53s and one closer to 54, making this one of the most closely watched US data points of the week.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics' measure of the gap between exports and imports of goods. A wider surplus is generally supportive for the Australian dollar, and the release is watched closely given China's status as Australia's largest trading partner.

The Reserve Bank of New Zealand's quarterly survey of businesses' and forecasters' expectations for inflation over the next two years. A rise in expectations reinforces the case for the RBNZ's recent pivot back to a tightening bias, and a high reading is generally supportive for the New Zealand dollar.

The main measure of consumer spending across the Eurozone. A high reading strengthens the euro, while a low one weakens it, since consumer demand is a key input into the ECB's growth and inflation outlook.

The number of people filing for unemployment benefits for the first time that week. A high frequency, early read on the US labour market, usually a minor mover unless it deviates sharply from expectations, and watched closely this week ahead of the following week's July jobs report.
